A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVA study. All 45 pages of v4 and 46 pages of v5, including appendices, equations and visual material, support reliable comparison despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original fine-tuning experiments on language tasks, VTAB-1K and Meta-World, together with empirical ablations and convergence analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and reports additional MiLoRA comparison results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The incremental activation-SVD initialization, zero initialization of B, explained-variance rank allocation and subsequent LoRA training remain unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 2 are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same common-sense tasks, MetaMathQA with GSM8K/MATH evaluation, Code-Feedback with coding benchmarks, GLUE, VTAB-1K and Meta-World. The expanded MiLoRA comparisons use retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: MiLoRA already appears in v4 Table 10's rank-16 ablation. v5 adds it to the common-sense, math and parameter-efficiency comparisons in Tables 7, 8 and 11 for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, tuning grids, metrics and decoding settings are retained. The expanded comparisons introduce no distinct evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The rank sweeps, EVA-minor and normalization comparisons, scale/direction ablations, initialization-distance studies and SVD batch-size/order analyses are retained. Their relocated or separated figures display existing analyses.

E5.justification: v5 Tables 7 and 14 explicitly report three-seed averaging and per-task standard deviations for MiLoRA's Llama-2-7B results, whose means already appeared without uncertainty in v4 Table 10. This adds uncertainty disclosure without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: v5 adds MiLoRA common-sense results for two more models and math results for three models; existing scores remain unchanged. For Gemma-2-9B, MiLoRA reports 83.7/41.9 on GSM8K/MATH versus EVA's retained 83.6/41.5, using 58.2M versus 55.9M trainable parameters (Tables 8 and 11).

T1.justification: New Section 3.4 substantially extends the theoretical scope to NTK-based generalization, introducing kernel definitions, weak-correlation and isotropic-gradient assumptions, and a spectral generalization-error argument in Equations 2–5. The original theorems and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The core initialization, adaptive-rank, convergence and cross-domain performance claims retain their scope. The added abstract sentence about a new Pareto frontier restates positioning already present in v4's introduction and contribution list.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly interprets EVA as approximating dominant NTK directions and reducing spectral-tail generalization error under simplifying assumptions. Existing empirical interpretations, applicability boundaries and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and runtime disclosures remain unchanged. The dedicated reproducibility appendix restates existing repository access; both the repository and PEFT documentation links remain available.

R1.justification: v5 adds a MiLoRA reference and its classification in Table 1, plus NTK-related citations to Jacot et al., Arora et al. and Lee et al. The existing related-work positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Limited abstract and prose edits accompany the new NTK subsection and reproducibility appendix. Affiliations and the publication header change, and the separate supplementary title and contents are removed. Most narrative text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: MiLoRA rows and plot legends are added. The GSM8K plot moves into the main text, while v4 Table 3 and Figure 10's similarity panel are combined in v5 Figure 5. Other displays are relocated; Table 8's best-score emphasis is not consistently updated.

improvement.justification: Expanded MiLoRA comparisons and uncertainty reporting improve empirical completeness. However, Section 4.2 retains the Gemma-GSM8K highest-score claim despite Table 8 reporting MiLoRA at 83.7 versus EVA at 83.6; EVA still uses fewer parameters. The new NTK argument also leaves the dimensional reduction from parameter-space covariance in Equation 3 to activation covariance in Equation 4 unexplained. These gains and new consistency and justification problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
